### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. spastic paraplegia 30A, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:888)

**Proposed mechanism:** KIF1A (HGNC:888) —DISRUPTS→ Axonal transport (GO:0008094); Axonal transport (GO:0008094) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal development (GO:0048666); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Spasticity (HP:0001257); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in KIF1A disrupt axonal transport, which in turn impairs neuronal development, leading to the shared phenotypes of spasticity, intellectual disability, and global developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a common pathogenic variant in KIF1A with a population frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD. _(variant: HGNC:888)_

**Why it matters:** Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring KIF1A function or improving axonal transport could potentially benefit patients with both conditions.

#### 2. spastic paraplegia 30B, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.785)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:888)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in KIF1A (HGVS:NG_007092.1:g.43297G>A) —DISRUPTS→ KIF1A (HGNC:888); KIF1A (HGNC:888) —DISRUPTS→ Axonal transport (GO:0006911); Axonal transport (GO:0006911) —LEADS_TO→ Spastic paraplegia (HP:0001257); Axonal transport (GO:0006911) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function variants in KIF1A disrupt axonal transport, leading to the shared phenotypes of spastic paraplegia and intellectual disability.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in KIF1A with a dominant-negative effect or a gain-of-function mechanism for either disease would falsify the proposed loss-of-function hypothesis. _(variant: Exome Variant Server (EVS) or gnomAD data showing a high allele frequency (>0.1%) for specific pathogenic variants associated with these diseases in the general population would also challenge the rare disease association.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of disrupted axonal transport due to KIF1A dysfunction can inform the development of targeted therapies for both MONDO:0013656 and spastic paraplegia 30B, potentially through strategies aimed at enhancing KIF1A function or mitigating the downstream consequences of impaired axonal transport.

#### 3. neuropathy, hereditary sensory, type 2C  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:888)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic KIF1A variant (null) —DISRUPTS→ KIF1A (HGNC:888); KIF1A (HGNC:888) —DISRUPTS→ Axonal transport (GO:0097062); Axonal transport (GO:0097062) —LEADS_TO→ Spastic paraplegia (HP:0001256); Axonal transport (GO:0097062) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003210). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in KIF1A that are associated with loss-of-function in one disease but gain-of-function in the other, or the discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of KIF1A in axonal transport provides a potential therapeutic target for both MONDO:0013656 and MONDO:0013634, as interventions aimed at restoring or enhancing axonal transport function could benefit patients with either condition.

#### 4. complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811434, Reactome:R-HSA-983189)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in TUBB2B (rsXXXXXXX) —DISRUPTS→ TUBB2B (HGNC:12002); TUBB2B (HGNC:12002) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule dynamics (GO:0007017); Microtubule dynamics (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal migration (GO:0001705); Neuronal migration (GO:0001705) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0002079); Neuronal migration (GO:0001705) —LEADS_TO→ Brain malformations (HP:0002079). Pathogenic variants in TUBB2B lead to disrupted microtubule dynamics, which in turn impairs neuronal migration, ultimately resulting in the phenotypes of cortical dysplasia and other brain malformations observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in TUBB2B with a minor allele frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD, or the identification of distinct causal genes for each disease that do not converge on microtubule dynamics or neuronal migration pathways, would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving TUBB2B and microtubule dysfunction in these distinct but related neurodevelopmental disorders could inform therapeutic strategies aimed at stabilizing microtubules or promoting proper neuronal migration, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 5. complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 5  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811434, Reactome:R-HSA-983189)

**Proposed mechanism:** KIF1A (HGNC:6412) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule dynamics and organization (GO:0007010); TUBB2A (HGNC:12590) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule dynamics and organization (GO:0007010); Microtubule dynamics and organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Microtubule dynamics and organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0002059); Microtubule dynamics and organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263). Haploinsufficiency of either KIF1A or TUBB2A disrupts normal microtubule dynamics and organization, leading to overlapping phenotypes of seizures, cortical dysplasia, and global developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in KIF1A or TUBB2A in patients diagnosed with either disease, or identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways being disrupted in each condition. _(variant: High frequency (>=1%) of pathogenic variants in KIF1A or TUBB2A in the general population (gnomAD).)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared impact of KIF1A and TUBB2A haploinsufficiency on microtubule dynamics could reveal common therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0013656 and complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 5, potentially leading to treatments that address the core neurological deficits.

#### 6. oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest 24  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.397)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811434, Reactome:R-HSA-983189)

**Proposed mechanism:** KIF1A (HGNC:6407) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule dynamics and axonal transport (GO:0007017); TUBA1C (HGNC:11676) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule dynamics and axonal transport (GO:0007017); Microtubule dynamics and axonal transport (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental disorder (HP:0001263); Microtubule dynamics and axonal transport (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (HP:0030174). Mutations in KIF1A and TUBA1C disrupt microtubule dynamics and axonal transport, leading to distinct but mechanistically related phenotypes of neurodevelopmental disorder and oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in KIF1A or TUBA1C exhibiting phenotypes unrelated to neuronal development or gamete/embryo maturation would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if variants in KIF1A/TUBA1C are found to be highly prevalent (e.g., >1% in gnomAD) in control populations without these specific phenotypes, it would suggest these genes are not the primary causal agents or that the observed phenotypes are polygenic. _(variant: gnomad_v2.1.1)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of KIF1A and TUBA1C in microtubule-dependent processes could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting cytoskeletal integrity or axonal transport that might benefit patients with either disease, particularly if early developmental processes are amenable to intervention.

#### 7. macrothrombocytopenia, isolated, 1, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.396)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811434, Reactome:R-HSA-983189)

**Proposed mechanism:** TUBB1 (HGNC:12172) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule organization and function (GO:0007010); Microtubule organization and function (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal megakaryocyte morphology (HP:0030146); Microtubule organization and function (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal platelet size (HP:0001873); Abnormal platelet size (HP:0001873) —LEADS_TO→ Macrothrombocytopenia (HP:0001885); Microtubule organization and function (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological abnormalities (HP:0000707). Haploinsufficiency of TUBB1 disrupts microtubule organization and function. In megakaryocytes, this leads to abnormal morphology and platelet size, resulting in macrothrombocytopenia (Disease B). In neurons, disruption of microtubule function leads to neurological abnormalities (Disease A).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants for MONDO:0013656 (KIF1A related) and MONDO:0800047 (TUBB1 related) are completely distinct and do not converge on any shared downstream pathway or process at a molecular level, or that the proposed haploinsufficiency of TUBB1 is not a contributing factor to MONDO:0013656. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in TUBB1 that are strongly associated with MONDO:0013656.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying shared pathways, even with distinct downstream effects, can reveal potential therapeutic targets that could modulate microtubule dynamics for treating neurological disorders and hematological conditions.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TUBB8 in microtubule dynamics offers potential for therapeutic strategies targeting fundamental cellular processes that, when disrupted, lead to distinct rare developmental disorders.

#### 9. facial palsy, congenital, with ptosis and velopharyngeal dysfunction  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.375)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811434, Reactome:R-HSA-983189)

**Proposed mechanism:** KIF1A (HGNC:6405) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal development (GO:0048666); TUBB6 (HGNC:27036) —DISRUPTS→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010); neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability (HP:0001249); cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ facial palsy, congenital, with ptosis, and velopharyngeal dysfunction (HP:0030160); neuronal development (GO:0048666) —INCREASES→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010). Loss-of-function mutations in KIF1A disrupt neuronal development, leading to intellectual disability. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TUBB6 disrupt cytoskeletal organization, contributing to facial palsy, ptosis, and velopharyngeal dysfunction. Both neuronal development and cytoskeletal organization are critical for overall neuronal function and are closely related processes, with cytoskeletal organization being essential for many aspects of neuronal development.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that mutations in KIF1A are exclusively associated with MONDO:0013656 and mutations in TUBB6 are exclusively associated with MONDO:0060589, with no overlap in affected cellular processes or pathways, this hypothesis would be falsified.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on KIF1A and TUBB6 for neuronal development and cytoskeletal integrity could reveal common therapeutic targets for interventions aimed at ameliorating neurological deficits in both conditions.
